description: A chief financial officer must authorize the transfer of a clean-energy tax-credit package and finalize the eligible credit amount, cash proceeds, closing date, and documentation actions, with input from the tax manager and treasury manager.

shared_context.S1: The company wants to monetize clean-energy tax credits generated by its completed battery-storage project.
shared_context.S2: The preliminary project schedule lists $5,000,000 of potentially transferable tax credits.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding decision on whether and how to transfer the credits.
shared_context.S4: Company approval policy requires the tax manager and treasury manager to give their sign-offs before the CFO authorizes a tax-credit transfer.

PF1.text: Ravi completed the tax-file review this morning and confirmed that only $4,200,000 is currently transferable; $800,000 remains unsupported by required wage and apprenticeship records. He has not yet updated the preliminary project schedule. The transfer also requires the substantiation package to be filed with the tax records within 10 business days of closing.

PF2.text: Maya received the buyer's executed term sheet yesterday and confirmed that the buyer will pay exactly $3,990,000 for the $4,200,000 eligible credit package, with funds settling on 2026-11-18. The term sheet requires a signed transfer certificate at settlement, but the terms have not yet been entered in the treasury workflow.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly $4,200,000 of eligible credits must be transferred.
The settlement must provide exactly $3,990,000 in cash proceeds.
The tax substantiation package must be filed within exactly 10 days of closing.
The settlement must include both the tax substantiation and signed transfer-certificate commitments.

content_checks.C6: any('substantiation' in c['detail'] and 'file' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any('transfer certificate' in c['detail'] and 'signed' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The preliminary schedule supports transferring $5,000,000, but PF1 changes the transferable amount to exactly $4,200,000, sets the substantiation deadline to exactly 10 days, and supplies the tax basis that must be cited.

Without PF2, the company has no confirmed executable buyer terms or settlement date; PF2 changes cash proceeds to exactly $3,990,000, fixes closing at 2026-11-18, and supplies the signed transfer-certificate commitment that makes authorization executable.
